messages:

Subject: Post-call: inference unit economics playbook — next asks & owners

Hi Leonard / Sara — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we heard, the levers we discussed, and suggested next steps so everyone is aligned. Let me know if I misstated anything.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: inference cost is the gating factor for your agent rollout (fractions of a cent multiply across high volume flows).
- Goal: launch a pilot for payments-reconciliation agents with target latency p95 < 300ms and a budget envelope of ~$25k/mo for initial pilot spend.
- Constraint: procurement prefers a short pilot (1–2 months) before committing to reserved capacity.

Key levers we discussed
- Batching (server-side continuous batching) to reduce per-token kernel overhead for short-turnaround calls.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context across sessions (your reconciliation flows have high prefix reuse).
- Model quantization + a smaller model variant for lower-cost inference in non-critical paths.

Quick rough economics we referenced on the call (back-of-envelope)
- Baseline: 1M sessions/mo * ~750 tokens/session => 750M tokens/mo. At a hosted list rate of $0.0003/token => ~$225k/mo.
- With batching + cache we estimated ~35–45% unit cost reduction for your workload profile => ~$125–150k/mo.
- With a short reserved pilot and model/quantization tuning we estimated further savings toward your target (~60% from baseline) but that requires a 4–6 week optimization cycle.

Actions I propose (owners & deadlines)
1) Redwood: deliver a pilot scope doc + measurement plan (who: Naomi) — by Tue, 11 May 2027.
2) Redwood: formal pilot estimate workbook (who: Marissa) — draft by Fri, 14 May 2027 (will include cost buckets: hosted vs dedicated, expected token burn, optimistic/likely/scenario rates).
3) Redwood: run sample throughput / latency sim using your sample traces (who: Aditya) — start by Wed, 12 May; results by Tue, 18 May.
4) CapitalPay: confirm budget band and procurement path / POC approval owner (who: Leonard / procurement) — by Mon, 17 May.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short workbook and a one-pager on batching mechanics to make the numbers transparent.

If that list looks correct I’ll send the pilot scope + measurement plan first thing tomorrow. Thanks again — Naomi

Thanks Naomi — appreciated the recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- The $25k/mo number is what our product team can sign off for a 6-week proof-of-value; procurement may be flexible if ROI is demonstrated quickly.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms is correct for the critical path (reconciliation core). For non-critical background jobs we can tolerate up to ~700ms.
- Typical session payload: 180 tokens in (prompt + metadata), ~600 tokens out (model summary + action suggestions) — closer to 780 tokens/session on average.

We’ll confirm procurement contact for the POC by Monday. Please include a breakout in the workbook that shows cost sensitivity to avg tokens/session and batch window (10ms, 20ms, 50ms). Also, please call out the path if we exceed the pilot budget (recommended throttles, fallback model variants).

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Leonard — thanks for the detail. Per Naomi’s ask I attached a first-pass pilot estimate workbook (CP_pilot_estimate_v1.xlsx) and a short notes doc on batching assumptions (redwood_batching_notes.pdf). Highlights from the worksheet: 

Pilot assumptions (sheet: Summary)
- Pilot length: 6 weeks (recommended)
- Pilot throughput: 1M sessions/mo equivalent (scaled to 6-week window)
- Token assumptions: 780 tokens/session avg -> ~780M tokens/mo equivalent
- Candidate approaches modeled: hosted burst, reserved dedicated small (4xA100 equiv), mixed (hosted + reserve fallback)

Estimated ranges (hosted baseline vs optimized)
- Hosted baseline (no batching/cache): ~$234k/mo equivalent for full run rate (shows why pilot is limited).
- Pilot (with expected batching + 30% prefix reuse): estimated pilot burn ~$110–135k for the 6-week equivalent (we model optimistic/likely/conservative).
- Optimized reserved + quantized variant: near-term run-rate that could approach ~$85–95k/mo after a 4–6 week tuning window (this assumes we can reach 50–60% batch/cache benefit on peak flows).

Sensitivity tabs included: tokens/session, batch window latency trade-off (10/20/50ms), cache hit rate (0/30/50%). We call out recommended telemetry to capture (per-request token counts, cache hit, queue wait time) so we can measure impact quickly.

Ask: Naomi — if you’re good with the scope I’ll finalize a formal pilot SOW and a short measurement rubric so procurement has clarity.

Notes: the workbook contains line items for incremental engineering support (edge adapters, small SDK changes) — we left those optional but flagged where they materially reduce cost.

—Marissa
